title.narrative: Enhancing Gender-Responsive Appropriately Adaptive Energy Technologies for Climate Resilience -Magwi County South Sudan

description.narrative: This project directly advances Christian Aid South Sudan’s strategic priority of promoting climate justice by delivering transformative, community-led climate adaptation solutions. It empowers women and girls through equitable access to clean energy technologies and inclusive decision-making process, while fostering resilient livelihoods by reducing reliance on unsustainable energy sources and enhancing food and income security. By integrating gender equity, environmental sustainability, and economic resilience, the project offers a scalable model for impactful, locally driven development. The project will use the energy waste (ashes) and kitchen residues to fertilize and protect women-led kitchen gardens and homestead trees. This unique energy innovation in the rural locality will reduce the burden on women and girls especially in their access to alternative cooking energy technologies, facilitate and empower them in the design and use of locally appropriate innovative low-cost energy technologies from biomass of agricultural, livestock and forest wastes. The project will promote healthy households and protected environment in the face of climate change. It will restore and nurture ecosystem in the locality. Ultimately, women/girls are empowered, energy, food and livelihood security enhanced, leading to climate-resilient people living in healthy environment. Therefore, given the urgent and intersecting challenges facing Magwi County—ranging from extreme energy poverty and climate vulnerability to entrenched gender inequality—there is a clear and compelling need for targeted, sustainable intervention. This project offers a transformative solution that not only addresses immediate humanitarian needs but also builds long-term resilience through gender-responsive, climate-adaptive energy technologies. By funding this initiative, Christian Aid and Base Net will catalyze meaningful change in one of South Sudan’s most underserved populations. The project aligns seamlessly with global development priorities, including the Sustainable Development Goals, and with Christian Aid’s strategic commitment to climate justice, gender equity, and resilient livelihoods. Project Objectives and Expected Results Outcome 1: Women and girls empowered through adoption of adaptive locally appropriate energy technologies for climate resilience Output 1.1. 100 women-headed households engaged in making and use of cost-effective improved energy-saving cook stoves Output 1.2. 100 women-headed households engaged in design and use of low-cost biomass energy briquettes from agricultural, livestock and forestry wastes Output 1.3. 100 women-headed households trained in use of biomass ash to fertilize and protect their kitchen / backyard gardens and homestead trees. Project location: Magwi Payam, Agoro Maji, Abara, Ayii, Obama and Nyolo
